title: The Detention of Westbrook High
premise: At Westbrook High, every senior answers the same college essay prompt — 'What did you inherit?' — and the best answer is performed at the Founders' Audition, a tradition that has defined the town for a century. Tamsin Lockridge, a baker's daughter who channels grief and joy into her bread, plans to write something safe and forgettable. But her essay accidentally exposes the truth about the Audition's founding: it was built on a betrayal that cost her grandmother everything, and the school board is using the centennial to end the tradition entirely. To save it, Tamsin must bake her family's buried memory into something the whole town can taste — and perform the most honest answer of her life at the final audition, knowing the truth might burn down the legacy she's trying to protect.
about_author: Petra Sandoval is a former high school debate coach who grew up above her family's panadería in a small mill town, where she learned that recipes are just stories you can eat. She writes about stubborn teenagers, small-town secrets, and the inheritance nobody asks for.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Senior year begins at Westbrook High, where the annual essay prompt is announced: 'What did you inherit?' Tamsin, who bakes her feelings into bread at her family's bakery, plans a bland answer about work ethic. When she tests a grief-loaf recipe that night, the smell unlocks a memory of her late grandmother she can't explain. Beat: the crack in her armor.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She drafts a safe, forgettable essay while navigating the social map of Westbrook: her best friend Dev's ambition, her mother's exhaustion, the bakery's quiet decline. A classmate, Priya Chandra, notices Tamsin flinch at the word 'inherit' and starts asking questions. Beat: the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: What the Bread Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Baking her grandmother's cardamom roll from a half-destroyed recipe card, Tamsin experiences a vivid sensory memory — a fire, a name she's never heard: 'Odell.' She writes it into her essay draft without thinking. Beat: memory as inheritance, whether invited or not.

chapters.title: The Centennial Committee
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, angling for valedictorian, joins the school board's Founders' Audition centennial committee and discovers the board plans to end the tradition after this year, calling it 'an expensive relic.' Dev keeps it quiet — information is leverage. Beat: ambition vs. loyalty.

chapters.title: Priya's Question
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Priya, the school paper's editor, corners Tamsin with an old yearbook photo: Tamsin's grandmother and a boy named Elias Odell, both listed as 'Audition Finalists, 1968' — but only Elias's name appears in the official record. Beat: the first hard evidence that the story has been edited.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Priya's alternating POV. They break into the school archive and find the 1968 audition program with her grandmother's name inked out. A custodian, Mr. Ferro, catches them — then quietly tells them his father was in that audience, and the winning performance that year was stolen. Beat: allies appear in unlikely places.

chapters.title: Mother's Silence
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin confronts her mother, who shuts down completely: 'Some bread doesn't rise, Tamsin. You throw it out and move on.' Her mother reveals only that the Audition 'took something' from Grandma Ruth. Beat: inherited silence as its own kind of wound.

chapters.title: Elias Odell, Still Alive
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya traces Elias Odell to a retirement community two towns over. Tamsin and Priya visit; Elias, sharp and bitter, tells them Ruth Lockridge wrote the performance that made the 1968 Audition legendary — and the school gave the credit to his family name to save face after a scandal. Beat: the betrayal takes shape.

chapters.title: The Stolen Score
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Elias explains: Ruth's piece, 'The Westbrook Reel,' was performed by him under pressure from the principal after Ruth was blamed for a kitchen fire she didn't cause. Ruth never baked publicly again — until she opened the bakery, quietly, for herself. Beat: understanding why her grandmother's recipes carry so much feeling.

chapters.title: Draft Zero
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin rewrites her essay with the truth — then panics and deletes it, submitting the safe version instead. Dev catches her at the bakery at 2 a.m. and, torn, admits what he knows about the board's plan to end the Audition. Beat: cowardice, and the first crack in Dev's ambition.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin decides to enter the Audition herself — not with the essay, but with a performance: baking 'The Westbrook Reel' as bread, live, with Ruth's story told through it. Priya agrees to investigate the fire cover-up; Dev, guilt-ridden, leaks the board's closure memo. Beat: commitment; the plan is set.

chapters.title: The Memo Goes Public
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya publishes the closure memo; the town erupts. Half of Westbrook wants the tradition saved out of nostalgia, the other half wants it gone out of embarrassment. Tamsin's mother, humiliated by the resurfaced fire story, forbids Tamsin from the Audition. Beat: the truth cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Burnt Offerings
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin defies her mother and practices the Reel bake; it fails repeatedly, because she's baking from the recipe card, not from memory. Mr. Ferro lets her use the school kitchen at night. Her mother finds out — and instead of exploding, sits down and asks to watch. Beat: the thaw.

chapters.title: What Ruth Wouldn't Say
chapters.summary: Mother's POV (first time). Tamsin's mother, Denise, remembers her own childhood: Ruth baking in furious silence, the one time she almost explained, the shame she passed down instead. Denise gives Tamsin Ruth's real recipe notebook, hidden in the attic — pages of notes in the margins that are clearly a confession. Beat: inheritance finally handed over.

chapters.title: The Marginalia
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The notebook's margins reveal the full truth: the 1968 fire was set by the principal's nephew to disqualify Ruth; the school knew and buried it. Ruth's last entry reads: 'Tell it with the bread. They'll listen with their mouths full.' Beat: the mission crystallizes — the Audition must become the confession.

chapters.title: Board of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev testifies before the school board, burning his valedictorian prospects by demanding the 1968 records be unsealed. The board chair, an Odell descendant, stonewalls — and quietly gets Tamsin disqualified from the Audition on a technicality. Beat: the establishment pushes back.

chapters.title: Disqualified
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Devastated, Tamsin nearly quits. Elias Odell arrives at the bakery with a solution: the Audition rules allow a 'legacy entry' — a finalist's descendant may perform on their behalf. Ruth was a finalist. Elias signs the paperwork with shaking hands. Beat: the door reopens, carried by the wronged party himself.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The bakery stays open all night as the town drifts in — Mr. Ferro, Priya, classmates, even board members — and Tamsin bakes test batches of the Reel, finally baking from memory instead of the card. Her mother works beside her without a word. Beat: quiet communion before the storm.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the centennial Audition, Tamsin performs: she bakes the Reel live on stage while telling Ruth's story, ending by handing warm pieces to the audience — including the board chair, who eats his family's stolen history and cannot speak. The hall rises. Beat: the climax; truth performed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. In the aftermath, the board chair resigns; the school unseals the 1968 records and restores Ruth Lockridge's name to the Audition plaque. The board votes to keep the tradition — restructured around honest inheritance rather than polished myth. Dev loses valedictorian and doesn't care. Beat: justice, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: Ruth's Name in Flour
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The bakery renames its signature roll 'The Ruth.' Tamsin submits a new college essay — the true one, unedited — and reads her grandmother's marginalia to a packed house at the re-dedication. Her mother cries for the first time in front of her. Beat: grief transformed into legacy.

chapters.title: What I Inherited
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. Acceptance letter in hand, Tamsin closes the bakery for a day and teaches Priya and Dev to bake the Reel, passing it on. The final essay prompt appears again for next year's seniors — 'What did you inherit?' — and Tamsin leaves her answer taped inside the flour bin for whoever needs it. Beat: survival's price paid, and worth it.
